Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, my father informed us: Abu Umamah narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma' al-Rahbi, from Thawban, who traced it to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without any need, the fragrance of Paradise is forbidden to her" [324] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/277.]].

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Najiyah narrated to us: Wahb ibn Munabbih narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Wasiti narrated to us: 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa, from 'Imarah ibn Rashid, from 'Ubadah ibn Nasi, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not divorce women except because of suspicion, for Allah, exalted is He, does not love those who constantly taste [divorce] nor those women who constantly taste [marriages]" [325] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 9/662, no. 27875, where it reads: 'do not divorce'.]].

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Hudhayfah Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali informed us: 'Abd al-Samad ibn Sa'id, judge of Homs, narrated to us: 'Abd al-Salam ibn al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Hadrami narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Khalid ibn Khalay informed us: my father narrated to us: Suwayd ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No believer swears by divorce [[In the source an addition: 'believer'.]], nor is he made to swear by it, except a hypocrite" [326] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 16/689, no. 46340.]].

﴿And count the 'iddah﴾, that is, count its number of menstrual cycles and preserve them.

﴿And fear Allah, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses﴾ until their waiting period is completed.

﴿Nor shall they [themselves] go out, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾, which is fornication, so that they may go out in order to have the legal punishment carried out upon them. This is the view of most of the commentators.

Qatadah said: its meaning is: he has the right to divorce her because of her disobedience (nushuz), so she may move from her husband's house. The "immorality" is disobedience.

Ibn 'Umar and al-Suddi said: her going out before the end of her waiting period is an immorality.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed me: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Musayyab narrated to us: Sa'id narrated to us: Sufayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾, he said: "Unless it becomes evident among her family; when it becomes evident among them, then it is permissible to expel her."

﴿These are the limits of Allah. Whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself. You know not; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some [new] matter﴾, that is, a reconciliation (murāja'ah) in the case of one or two [divorces], as long as she is in the waiting period.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, reading it to him: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Mutayri narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us: Haythам narrated to us, from Mughirah and Husayn 'Abd al-Rahman and Ash'ath and Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid and Dawud ibn Abi Hind and Shaban and Mujalid, all from al-Sha'bi, who said: I entered upon Fatimah bint Qays in Medina and asked her about the judgment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). She said: "My husband divorced me with a final (batta) divorce; I brought a case against him before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning housing and maintenance, but he did not assign me housing or maintenance, and he commanded me to observe my 'iddah in the house of Ibn Umm Maktum."

Haythам said: Mujalid said in his narration: "Maintenance and housing are only for the one who has the right of reconciliation."

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, saying: 'Aqil ibn Muhammad al-Faqih informed us that Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi, the judge, informed them, from Muhammad ibn Juhayr, from Ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Thawr, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah, that Fatimah bint Qays was married to Abu 'Amr ibn Hafs ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi, and that he went out with 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, to Yemen when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed him over part of Yemen. He sent to his wife Fatimah bint Qays a divorce that remained for her from her divorce, and he commanded 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah and al-Harith ibn Hisham to provide maintenance for her. They said to her: "By Allah, you have no maintenance except if you are pregnant."

She went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned to him what they had said. He did not assign her maintenance unless she was pregnant, and she asked his permission to move, and he permitted her. She said: "Where shall I move to, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "To Ibn Umm Maktum's." [327] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/417.]] He was blind; she would take off her clothes at his place and he would not see her. She remained there until her waiting period ended. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) married her to Usamah ibn Zayd. Marwan ibn al-Hakam sent Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb to her to ask her about this hadith. Marwan said: "We have not heard this hadith except from a woman; we will hold to the consensus (ʿişma) upon which we found the people." When Fatimah heard the words of Ibn Marwan, she said: "Between me and you is the Qur'an. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do not expel them from their houses﴾ up to His saying ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some [new] matter﴾." She said: "This is for the one who has the right of reconciliation; so what new matter can occur after three [divorces]?" [[Sahih Muslim: 4/197.]]

﴿And when they have reached their term﴾, that is, they have come near the end of their waiting period and are close to it.

﴿Then either retain them according to what is reasonable (bi-ma'ruf)﴾ by a reconciliation that you undertake, ﴿or part from them according to what is reasonable﴾, that is, leave them until their waiting period ends, so that they are with you and yet they are more in control of themselves.

﴿And do not harm them﴾, so that the harm is the opposite of what is reasonable.

﴿And bring two just witnesses from among you﴾ to the reconciliation and the separation.

﴿And establish the testimony for Allah. That is instructed to whoever should believe in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out﴾. 'Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak said: whoever divorces according to the Sunnah, "He will make for him a way out" is the possibility of reconciliation.

﴿And will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾, that is, from where he does not hope or anticipate.

Most of the commentators said: This verse was revealed concerning 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ash'ari. The polytheists had captured his son, called Salim, so he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the enemy has captured my son, and he also complained to him of poverty." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The family of Muhammad has nothing for the evening except a mudd (measure of food). So fear Allah, be patient, and recite much: 'There is no power and no might except through Allah.'" [328] [[I'anat al-Talibin: 4/389.]] The man did so. While he was in his house, his son came to him, the enemy having been careless about him, and he had taken camels and brought them to his father, who was poor. Al-Kalbi, in the narration of Yusuf ibn Malik, said: his son came with fifty camels.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Amir al-Balkhi informed us: al-Qasim ibn 'Abbad narrated to us: Salih ibn Muhammad al-Tirmidhi narrated to us: Abu 'Ali Ghalib narrated to us, from Sallam ibn Sulaym, from 'Abd al-Hamid, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ash'ari came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the enemy has captured my son, and his mother has become distressed, so what do you command me?" He said: "[Fear Allah and be patient], and I command you and her to recite much: 'There is no power and no might except through Allah.'" He returned to her, and she said: "What did the Prophet (ﷺ) tell you?" He said: "He commanded me and you to recite much: 'There is no power and no might except through Allah.'" She said: "How excellent is what he commanded you." So they both recited it. The enemy became careless about him, and he drove off their sheep, and he brought them to his father; they numbered four thousand sheep. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out and will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾, referring to what he drove off of the spoils [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/160; and Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 289, the words in brackets are from them.]].

Muqatil said: He obtained sheep and goods, then returned to his father. His father went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of the matter, and asked for permission for him to be lawful, and that he eat what his son had brought him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Yes," and Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shaybah narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ishaq informed us: 'Amr ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us: Sa'd ibn Rashid al-Hanafi narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out and will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾, and said: "A way out from the doubts of this world, from the agonies of death, and from the hardships of the Day of Resurrection" [330] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/232.]].

Ibn Mas'ud and Masruq said: ﴿He will make for him a way out﴾ means that he knows it is from Allah, and that Allah is his provider, and He is the giver and the withholder. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym: "a way out" from everything that is tight upon people. Abu al-'Aliyah: "a way out" from every hardship. Al-Hasan: "a way out" from what He has forbidden him. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: "whoever fears Allah" in performing the obligations, "He will make for him a way out" from punishment, "and will provide him" with reward "from where he does not expect."

Al-Sadiq said: "And will provide for him from where he does not expect," meaning: He will bless for him in what He has given him [331] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/43.]].

Sahl said: "And whoever fears Allah" in following the Sunnah, "He will make for him a way out" from the punishment of the people of innovation, "and will provide him Paradise from where he does not expect."

'Amr ibn 'Uthman al-Sada'i said: whoever stops at His limits and reckons His disobedience, He will bring him out from the unlawful to the lawful, from narrowness to ease, and from the Fire to Paradise.

Abu Sa'id al-Kharraz said: whoever disowns his own power and strength by returning to Him, "He will make for him a way out" from what He has charged him with, by helping him.

'Ali ibn Salih said: "He will make for him a way out" by making him content with his provision. It was also said: "Whoever fears Allah" regarding provision and other things, by cutting off attachments, "He will make for him a way out" through sufficiency, "and will provide him from where he does not expect."

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Makki ibn Malik al-Mut'i informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us: Mu'tamir narrated to us, from Kahmas, from Abu al-Sulayl, from Abu Dhar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I know a verse which, if people took hold of it, would suffice them: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out and will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾." So he kept repeating it and reciting it again and again [332] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/160.]].

It is related that a man came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "Appoint me to some office of what Allah has entrusted you with!" He said: "Do you recite the Qur'an?"

"He said: No. He said: We do not appoint one who does not recite the Qur'an. So the man left and strove to learn the Qur'an, hoping that he would return to 'Umar and be given a post. When he had learned the Qur'an, he stayed away from 'Umar. One day 'Umar saw him and said: O man, you have abandoned us. He said: O Commander of the Faithful, I am not one who abandons, but I have learned the Qur'an, and God Most High has made me independent of 'Umar and of the gate of 'Umar. He said: Which verse made you independent? He said: The words of God Most High: ﴿And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾.

Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad related to us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Adus related to us; 'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Razi related to us; Mahdi ibn Ja'far al-Ramli related to us; al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us from al-Hakam ibn Mus'ab from Muhammad ibn 'Ali from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas from his father from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever frequently seeks forgiveness, God will make for him a relief from every distress, a way out from every hardship, and will provide for him from where he does not expect" [333] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/248.]].

﴿And whoever relies upon God, He is sufficient for him﴾: that is, one who trusts in Him and whose heart is at rest in Him, in what is present and what is absent.

﴿God will surely accomplish His purpose﴾. The majority recited ﴿bāligh﴾ with tanwin and ﴿amrahu﴾ with a fatha: meaning, He carries out His command, executed within the circle of His decree. Ṭalḥa ibn Muḍarrib recited ﴿bāligu amrihi﴾ with the idafa (construct), and Ḥafs and al-Mufaḍḍal related the same from ʿĀṣim.

Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind recited ﴿bāligun﴾ with tanwin and ﴿amruhu﴾ with a ḍamma (nominative).

al-Farrā' said: that is, "His command is accomplishing."

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Nāfiʿ said: When ﴿And whoever relies upon God, He is sufficient for him﴾ was revealed, the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God is sufficient for us if we rely upon Him. So we forget what was ours and do not memorize it." Then God Most High revealed ﴿God will surely accomplish His purpose﴾, meaning: among you and upon you.

﴿God has set a measure for everything﴾: a limit and a term at which it ends.

Masruq said: In this verse, "God will surely accomplish His purpose" applies whether one relies upon Him or not, except that the one who relies upon Him, ﴿He will remove from him his misdeeds and enlarge his reward﴾.

al-Rabīʿ said: God Most High has decreed upon Himself that whoever relies upon Him, He suffices him; whoever believes in Him, He guides him; whoever lends to Him, He repays him; whoever trusts in Him, He saves him; and whoever calls upon Him, He answers him. The confirmation of this is in the Book of God Most High:

﴿And whoever believes in God, He guides his heart, and whoever relies upon God, He is sufficient for him. And if you lend to God a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you, and whoever holds fast to God has been guided to a straight path. And when My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near...﴾

﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months, and likewise those who have not yet menstruated.﴾ Some people said: "If you doubt" means: if you are uncertain whether the blood that appears from her is the blood of puberty, of menstruation, or of istihada (irregular bleeding). Others said: "If you are in doubt" concerns their age: you do not know what their age of puberty is in their waiting period, so their waiting period is three months. This is the saying of al-Zuhrī and Ibn Zayd.

Abu Saʿid Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ḥamdūn related to us; Abu Ḥātim Makkī ibn ʿAydān related to us; Abu al-Azhar Aḥmad ibn al-Azhar related to us; Asbāṭ ibn Muḥammad related to us from Muṭarrif from Abu ʿUthmān ʿAmr ibn Sālim, who said: When the waiting periods of women were revealed in Surat al-Baqara concerning the divorced and widowed women, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: "O Messenger of God, some people of Madina say that there remain women about whom nothing has been mentioned." He said: "And what are they?" He said: "The young, the old, and pregnant women." Then these verses were revealed: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation...﴾ to the end.

Muqātil said: When the verse ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾ was revealed, Khallād ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Qays al-Anṣārī said: "O Messenger of God, what is the waiting period of one who does not menstruate, of one who has not yet menstruated, and of a pregnant woman?" Then God Most High revealed: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation﴾, meaning the postmenopausal women who have ceased menstruating.

﴿If you are in doubt﴾: you are uncertain about their condition and their ruling.

Abu ʿAlī al-Zuhrī said: ﴿If you are in doubt﴾ means: if you are obstinate. He said: It is one of the words with opposite meanings, meaning both doubt and certainty, like "ẓann" (supposition). ﴿Their waiting period is three months, and likewise those who have not yet menstruated﴾, meaning the young girls.

﴿And for those with loads [of pregnancy], their term is that they should lay down their burden﴾ among the divorced and the widowed.

He said: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ḥamdūn related to us; Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ḥasan related to us; Muhammad ibn Yaḥyā related to us; ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us; Maʿmar related to us from al-Zuhrī from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUtba, who said: Marwān sent ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUtba to Subay'a bint al-Ḥārith to ask her about what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had informed her. She told him that she had been married to Saʿd ibn Khawla, who died while she was with him during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and that he had been [away], and she gave birth to her child before four months and ten days had passed since her husband's death, and then she was proposed to. She said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned what Abu al-Sanābil had said. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You have been released once you have given birth to your burden" [334] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/432; Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 9/651, no. 27821.]], and he commanded her to marry.

If a woman's menstruation has ceased while she is young, will she be made to wait to see whether she is pregnant or not? If her pregnancy becomes evident, her term is that she lay down her burden. If her pregnancy does not become evident, the jurists differed on this:

Some of them said: she is to be made to wait, and the most that is required is one year. This is the position of Mālik, Aḥmad, Isḥāq and Abū ʿUbayd, who held that the waiting period of a woman whose menstruation has ceased while she is young is one year, and they related this from ʿUmar and others.

As for the people of Iraq, they hold that her waiting period is three menstrual cycles, after she has menstruated once in her life, even if she remains twenty years until she reaches an age at which she despairs of menstruation; then her waiting period after despair is three months. This is the more sound position in the school of al-Shāfiʿī, and the scholars follow it, and they related this from Ibn Masʿūd and his companions.

﴿And whoever fears God, He will make for him ease in his affair. That is the command of God, which He has sent down to you. And whoever fears God, He will remove from him his misdeeds and enlarge his reward.﴾ ﴿Let them dwell﴾, meaning the divorced women of your wives,

﴿where you dwell﴾, that is, in the places where you live.

al-Kisā'ī said: ﴿min﴾ is an extraneous (metaphorically used) particle: "Let them dwell where you dwell," the divorced women of your wives.

﴿According to your means﴾: your ability and capacity. The common reading has a ḍamma on the wāw; al-Aʿraj read it with a fatḥa, and Nūḥ related from Yaʿqūb a kasra on the wāw; all are dialectal variants. ﴿Until their waiting period ends.﴾

﴿And do not harm them to constrain them﴾: do not injure them, so that you constrain their dwellings and they are forced out.

﴿And if they are pregnant, spend on them until they lay down their burden﴾, so that they may leave their waiting period.

The jurists differed on this question. Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, al-Awzāʿī, Ibn Abī Layla, Abū ʿUbayda and Muḥammad ibn Jarīr held that the irrevocably divorced woman (divorced three times) has no maintenance, but she has residence, arguing that God Most High generalized residence to all divorced women and specified maintenance only for pregnant women, saying ﴿spend on them until they lay down their burden﴾.

Aḥmad and Abū Thawr said: she has neither residence nor maintenance. They argued from the hadith of Fāṭima bint Qays, sister of al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays, when her husband, of the Makhzūm, sent her divorce, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not assign her maintenance, and said to her: "Maintenance is only due when he has the right of return over you," and he commanded her to observe her waiting period in the house of Ibn Umm Maktūm. We have mentioned this, and this is the view of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Zayd ibn Thābit [[See Sharḥ Muslim by al-Nawawī: 10/96.]].

As for [Sufyān] and the people of Iraq, they said: she has residence and maintenance, whether pregnant or not, and this is the view of ʿĀʾisha, may God be pleased with her.

It is related that ʿĀʾisha said to Fāṭima bint Qays: "Fear God, O Fāṭima; you have caused confusion among the people. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) only removed you because you were a woman with a sharp tongue, and he feared your tongue against your [in-laws]."

As for the maintenance of a pregnant woman whose husband has died, ʿAlī, Ibn ʿUmar, Sharīḥ, al-Nakhaʿī, al-Shaʿbī, Ḥammād, Ibn Abī Layla, [Sufyān] [[Thus in the manuscript; perhaps it is Sufyān al-Thawrī, though we have not found it in these words in the books of jurisprudence. However, in al-Mughnī he said: this was also the view of Ibn Shubruma, Ibn Abī Layla, al-Thawrī, al-Ḥasan, Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions, al-Batti and al-ʿAnbarī (al-Mughnī: 9/289).]] and his companions said: she is to be provided for from the entire estate until she gives birth.

Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allah, Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfa said: she is not to be provided for except from her own share [[See al-Mabsūṭ of al-Sarakhsī: 5/201.]].
